papers.title: Active Learning from Positive and Unlabeled Data
papers.abstract: During recent years, active learning has evolved into a popular paradigm for utilizing user's feedback to improve accuracy of learning algorithms. Active learning works by selecting the most informative sample among unlabeled data and querying the label of that point from user. Many different methods such as uncertainty sampling and minimum risk sampling have been utilized to select the most informative sample in active learning. Although many active learning algorithms have been proposed so far, most of them work with binary or multi-class classification problems and therefore can not be applied to problems in which only samples from one class as well as a set of unlabeled data are available.   Such problems arise in many real-world situations and are known as the problem of learning from positive and unlabeled data. In this paper we propose an active learning algorithm that can work when only samples of one class as well as a set of unlabelled data are available. Our method works by separately estimating probability desnity of positive and unlabeled points and then computing expected value of informativeness to get rid of a hyper-parameter and have a better measure of informativeness./ Experiments and empirical analysis show promising results compared to other similar methods.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于主动学习在仅正例和无标注数据分类中的方法，与FEA代理建模、生物力学或植入物设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses active learning for positive-unlabeled classification, with no connection to finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanical design.

summary_en.motivation: Active learning typically assumes fully labeled data, yet many real-world scenarios only have positive and unlabeled samples, motivating a method tailored for this setting.
summary_en.method: The proposed algorithm separately estimates probability densities of positive and unlabeled points and computes expected informativeness to avoid a hyper-parameter.
summary_en.result: Empirical results demonstrate improved performance over existing active learning methods on positive-unlabeled data.
summary_en.validation: Experimental comparison with baselines on synthetic and real datasets.

papers.title: Higher order Quasi-Monte Carlo integration for Bayesian Estimation
papers.abstract: We analyze combined Quasi-Monte Carlo quadrature and Finite Element approximations in Bayesian estimation of solutions to countably-parametric operator equations with holomorphic dependence on the parameters as considered in [Cl.~Schillings and Ch.~Schwab: Sparsity in Bayesian Inversion of Parametric Operator Equations. Inverse Problems, {\bf 30}, (2014)]. Such problems arise in numerical uncertainty quantification and in Bayesian inversion of operator equations with distributed uncertain inputs, such as uncertain coefficients, uncertain domains or uncertain source terms and boundary data. We show that the parametric Bayesian posterior densities belong to a class of weighted Bochner spaces of functions of countably many variables, with a particular structure of the QMC quadrature weights: up to a (problem-dependent, and possibly large) finite dimension $S$ product weights can be used, and beyond this dimension, weighted spaces with so-called SPOD weights are used to describe the solution regularity. We establish error bounds for higher order Quasi-Monte Carlo quadrature for the Bayesian estimation based on [J.~Dick, Q.T.~LeGia and Ch.~Schwab, Higher order Quasi-Monte Carlo integration for holomorphic, parametric operator equations, Report 2014-23, SAM, ETH Zürich]. It implies, in particular, regularity of the parametric solution and of the countably-parametric Bayesian posterior density in SPOD weighted spaces. This, in turn, implies that the Quasi-Monte Carlo quadrature methods in [J. Dick, F.Y.~Kuo, Q.T.~Le Gia, D.~Nuyens, Ch.~Schwab, Higher order QMC Galerkin discretization for parametric operator equations, SINUM (2014)] are applicable to these problem classes, with dimension-independent convergence rates $\calO(N^{-1/p})$ of $N$-point HoQMC approximated Bayesian estimates, where $0<p<1$ depends only on the sparsity class of the uncertain input in the Bayesian estimation.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文为贝叶斯估计中拟蒙特卡罗积分提供理论误差分析，但未涉及任何生物医学或植入物设计应用。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address any implant or biomedical application, does not provide a surrogate model for FEA, and lacks any experimental or simulation case study relevant to biomechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 分析贝叶斯估计中参数算子方程的拟蒙特卡罗积分误差。
summary_zh.method: 结合拟蒙特卡罗求积与有限元近似，推导加权Bochner空间中的正则性。
summary_zh.result: 获得维数无关的收敛速度，依赖于输入稀疏性。
summary_zh.validation: 纯理论推导，无数值实验。

summary_en.motivation: To analyze error bounds for Quasi-Monte Carlo integration in Bayesian estimation of parametric operator equations.
summary_en.method: Combined Quasi-Monte Carlo quadrature with finite element approximations, establishing regularity in weighted Bochner spaces.
summary_en.result: Derived dimension-independent convergence rates depending on the sparsity class of uncertain inputs.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical analysis only, without numerical experiments.
